analysis:
Both changed files are test-only. SegmentedFleetGeometry.swift head lines 45-48 change the gpt-oss-20b fixture dtypes from [bf16]+23×fp32 to 24×bf16, justified by an SDK change. EngineV2PrefixCacheWiringTests.swift head lines 435-436 and 445 change comments only; the assertions are unchanged, including the contiguous GPT-OSS fallback of nominal+2048 (line 443).

There is no production change, so I identified no new attack surface. The relevant production behavior is KV sizing and admission, which bears on availability (T-029) and on T-041's no-persistent-carve posture for the prefix cache. That code, mainly EngineV2SlotFactory.slotKVBytesPerToken with nativeLayerDTypes, lives in other batch files not supplied here.

One cross-file question remains for integration. If production now uses observed native dtypes for GPT-OSS, admission budgeting could under-reserve memory should the real dtypes be fp32. That could cause memory pressure or OOM, an availability issue for the provider. The head comment says the conservative fp32 delta applies only without observed native types, which implies production gained an observed-types path.

Even so, the test fixture alone is not evidence of a regression. The relevant threat context (T-041 staging reservations, T-029) contains no confidentiality or authorization impact from this change.
